chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the Muslim is overcome by the weakness of old age, God, Mighty and Majestic, commands the angel to record for him in that state of his the like of what he used to do when he was young, energetic, and healthy.'
And similarly when he falls ill, God assigns an angel to him who writes for him during his illness what he used to do of the good in his good health, until God raises him and takes him (death).
And similar to that is the disbeliever: when he is afflicted with sickness in his body, God writes for him what he used to do of evil in his good health.

key_terms.سُقْم: Sickness, illness — used for the incapacitating condition that prevents normal action
key_terms.ضَعْفُ الْكِبَرِ: Weakness of old age — the physical frailty that prevents performance of acts of worship and good deeds
key_terms.وَكَّلَ: Assigns/appoints — God directly delegates an angel with a specific task, emphasizing divine attentiveness
key_terms.يَرْفَعَهُ: Raises him — a euphemism for death, indicating the soul's elevation to God at death

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim still receive reward for good deeds they can no longer perform due to old age or illness?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS) from the Prophet (SAWW), addresses the divine mercy shown to aging and ill believers. The Prophet teaches that when a Muslim can no longer perform the good deeds of youth due to old age or illness, God records those deeds as if they were still being performed, preserving the full reward. Conversely, the disbeliever is similarly held accountable — his evil deeds continue to be recorded during his illness, reflecting the principle of divine justice: each soul receives what its intentions and habitual acts merit.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, 
(It has been narrated) from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the Muslim is overcome by weakness of the old age, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commands the Angel that he should record for him during that state of his, similar to what he would have done had he been young, energetic, healthy.

And similar to that is when he is sick, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Allocates two Angels with him, to write for him during his sickness what he would have done from the goodness during his good health, until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Raises him, and Captures him (death).
And similar to that is the Infidel, when he labours with sickness in his body, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes down for him what he would have done, from the evil (deeds), during his well-being’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy Prophet has said, ‘
When a Muslim is weakened due to old age, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, commands an angel to write down for him of good deeds equal to what he did when young, vigorous and in good health.

Similarly, when he becomes ill, Allah commands an angel to write down for him during his illness of good deeds equal to what he performed in good health up to the time Allah raises him and takes him (away) from this life.
In the case of an unbeliever, in his illness Allah writes down against him of evil deeds equal to what he would commit when in good health.’”
